_meta.purpose: Machine-readable contract for the agentic SLO-gated promotion pipeline. Consumed by the observability-slo-engine crate family, the governance-promotion-readiness CI lane, and the cloud-ci promotion jobs.

industry_baseline.burn_rate_model: Google SRE Workbook ch. 5 multi-window multi-burn-rate

mimir_multi_tenancy.enforcement: server-side at Mimir distributor; client-side filtering NOT relied upon

deployment_salt.storage: OpenBao kv-v2; one salt per Mimir cluster

sli_types_supported.indicator_template: <service-defined>; e.g. consistency-check pass-rate over rolling window
<service-defined>; e.g. event-age max over rolling window for stream processors

alert_burn_rates.name: budget-exhausted
alert_burn_rates.rationale: 100% budget exhausted over the full window

promotion_eligibility_ledger.rationale: Ledger storage in Mimir time-series (not git-tracked JSONL) per 2026-05-17 user decision. At hyperscaler scale (10k+ µservices × 60s evaluator cadence × per-environment) a single JSONL file would grow ~14M records/day; Mimir is purpose-built for this cardinality and the burn-rate evaluator is already querying Mimir for SLI signal. Queries are PromQL. The audit trail is the Mimir block-storage history (object-storage-backed retention) plus active typed quality-gate / cloud-ci evidence artifacts for the change; standalone multispectrum evidence-file emission is retired.

metric_emissions.name: promotion_eligibility_verdict
metric_emissions.value: 1 for current verdict; 0 for prior verdicts (staleness flag)

metric_emissions.name: promotion_release_pointer_current
metric_emissions.value: 1 for current release pointer; carries SHA in label for query addressability

metric_emissions.name: promotion_release_pointer_prior
metric_emissions.value: 1 for prior pointer (used by rollback primitive)

recording_rules_summary.purpose: the latest verdict per (microservice, target_env); consumed by governance-promotion-readiness lane

recording_rules_summary.expr: min by (source_sha, target_env) (count by (microservice, source_sha, target_env, verdict) (promotion_eligibility_verdict{verdict="eligible"}))
recording_rules_summary.purpose: 1 iff every microservice touched by the SHA is eligible

promotion_eligibility_ledger.query_api: PromQL via Mimir HTTP /prometheus/api/v1/query and /api/v1/query_range endpoints; auth via Mimir multi-tenant API key for the CI tenant.
promotion_eligibility_ledger.retention: Mimir long-term storage backed by object storage (S3-compatible); default 90 days hot + 2 years cold-tier (configurable per /specs/observability-retention.json future spec).
promotion_eligibility_ledger.audit_evidence: Promotion-time burn-rate snapshots are archived through active typed quality-gate / cloud-ci evidence artifacts and referenced audit-chain rows when required. The former per-changeset multispectrum evidence-file convention is retired with the bespoke admission-adapter path and is historical provenance only.

release_pointer_convention.deprecation_note: tree-wide single staging/production refs deprecated by ADR-0139; retained read-only for legacy compatibility until all microservices migrate.

transitions.trigger: all burn-rate alerts not firing for the (microservice, source_sha, target_env)
OpenSLO manifest missing or invalid for the microservice
OpenSLO manifest missing or invalid for the microservice
post-promotion production-tier fast-burn alert fires within 1h of promotion

gate_state_machine.fail_closed_rationale: absence of an OpenSLO manifest, evaluator outage, or unparseable signal all default to 'held' rather than 'eligible' so the gate never permits unevaluated promotion

evaluator.rejected_alternative_implementation: scheduled GitHub Action against Prometheus snapshots — rejected as primary; retained as bootstrap fallback only
evaluator.idempotency: ledger writes keyed on (microservice, source_sha, target_env); duplicate evaluations append a no-op record only when verdict changes

promote_workflow_contract.primary_trigger: signed eligibility-changed event consumed by cloud-ci promotion job
preconditions: governance-promotion-readiness CI check green for source SHA on target environment
burn-rate evaluator has emitted at least one record for (microservice, source_sha, target_env) and the latest verdict is 'eligible'
source ref's commits are signed (existing required-check invariant)
actions: if eligible verdict — call audited release-pointer advancement primitive with source HEAD and expected prior pointer
the primitive verifies fast-forward ancestry, signed source commits, protected-ref policy, and latest eligible verdict before updating the release pointer
promote_workflow_contract.downstream_trigger: advancing release/<microservice>/staging emits signed eligibility-changed event for the production tier

rollback_primitive.trigger: production-tier fast-burn alert fires within 1h post-promotion AND verdict transitions eligible → rollback
rollback_primitive.action: call audited release-pointer rollback primitive to advance release/<microservice>/production back to the prior recorded pointer for that microservice
rollback_primitive.ledger_record: append rollback verdict and from_sha/to_sha to the audit-chain plus Mimir-backed promotion ledger
rollback_primitive.incident_emission: RollbackExecuted event consumed by grafana-oncall; incident raised with priority 'major'
rollback_primitive.post_rollback_state: microservice held until burn-rate clears and new commit lands

canary_cohort_weighting.implementation: service-mesh traffic-split per microservice (Istio VirtualService weighted routing or equivalent)

ramp_steps.exit_criterion: no fast-burn, slow-burn, or ticket-burn alert

canary_cohort_weighting.abort_on: any burn-rate alert; immediately drain canary cohort to 0%

ci_lane_contract.name: governance-promotion-readiness
ci_lane_contract.added_to: planned for cloud-ci/GitHub required checks on dev and staging; not live until IP-012 implementation and required-check configuration merge
behaviour: enumerate every microservice touched by the source SHA (via path-based ownership: a change to microservices/<ms>/** is owned by <ms>)
for each microservice, read the latest record in registry/promotion-eligibility.jsonl for (microservice, source_sha, target_env)
exit 0 only when every microservice has an 'eligible' verdict
exit non-zero with structured JSON listing which microservices are held|rejected|rollback and the burn-rate snapshot
ci_lane_contract.implementation: cargo run -p dev-cli -- gate validate governance-promotion-readiness --sha <sha> --env <env>

bootstrap_order_decision.policy: incremental — each microservice brings its OpenSLO manifest at the time it migrates to microservices/<ms>/ per ADR-0131. Until a microservice has a manifest, the gate treats its eligibility as 'held' (fail-closed) and that microservice cannot promote past 'dev'.
bootstrap_order_decision.rationale: hyperscaler practice (Google SRE: SLOs precede production traffic); also forces the SLO-authoring discipline rather than back-loading it

backfill_replay_contract.replay_trigger: manual via `cargo run -p dev-cli -- promotion replay-eligibility`
backfill_replay_contract.replay_immutability_invariant: replay appends new verdict record; never mutates original

canary_cohort_weighting_finalized.service_mesh_implementation: Istio VirtualService weighted routing per pack (latest LTS per docs/standards/observability-slo.md §'Container + orchestration')

ramp_steps.exit_criterion: no fast-burn, slow-burn, or ticket-burn alert

canary_cohort_weighting_finalized.abort_on: any burn-rate alert; immediately drain canary cohort to 0%
